subproblem.title: Tangent planes, measurability and density of a rectifiable varifold (Simon Ch. 3, 1.2-1.9)
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, U an open subset of R^(n+l) and V = v(M,theta) a RectifiableVarifold n l U (M = V.carrier contained in U, countably n-rectifiable and H^n-null-measurable; theta = V.mult positive on M, H^n-measurable on M, with integral_{M cap K} theta dH^n < infinity for every compact K contained in U). Let mu = V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M and p_x = V.tangentProj x (orthogonal projection onto the approximate tangent space of M with respect to theta at x where it exists, 0 otherwise). Then (a) for mu-a.e. x there is an n-dimensional subspace P with p_x = orthogonal projection onto P; (b) x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable; (c) for mu-a.e. x, mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x) as r -> 0+ (V.HasDensity x (theta x)).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ), 1 ≤ n → ∀ (U : Set (Amb n ℓ)), IsOpen U → ∀ V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ U, (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, ∃ P : Submodule ℝ (Amb n ℓ), Module.finrank ℝ P = n ∧ V.tangentProj x = P.starProjection) ∧ AEStronglyMeasurable V.tangentProj V.weight ∧ (∀ᵐ x ∂V.weight, V.HasDensity x (V.mult x))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2 (with Ch. 2, Thm 1.5), Remark 1.3, the proof of Theorem 1.6 ('=>'), Remarks 1.8(1),(2) and Theorem 1.9 ('=>'), localized to U (theta is only integrable on compact subsets of U), together with the measurability statement (F1) of the parent proof.

Notation: mu := V.weight; p_x := V.tangentProj x; B_r(x) is the closed ball; H^n = mu_HE[n]; for f in C_c(R^(n+l)), x in R^(n+l) and lambda > 0, Lambda_lambda(f) := integral_{eta_{x,lambda}(M)} f(y) theta(x + lambda y) dH^n(y), where eta_{x,lambda}(z) = (z - x)/lambda (the quantity in Definition 1.7, i.e. in SimonGMT Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x P).

1. Reduction. mu(A) = integral_{A cap M} theta dH^n and theta > 0 on M, so mu(E) = 0 whenever H^n(E cap M) = 0; hence it suffices to prove (a), (b), (c) for H^n-a.e. x in M (for (b): a map that agrees with a strongly measurable map outside such a set is mu-a.e. strongly measurable). Since U is open, fix open balls W_1, W_2, ... with compact closures cl(W_m) contained in U and union equal to U. Then mu_m := mu restricted to cl(W_m) is a finite Borel regular measure (mu(cl W_m) = integral_{M cap cl W_m} theta dH^n < infinity by V.integrableOn_mult), and it suffices to treat x in M cap W_m for each m. Since theta is H^n-a.e. measurable on M (V.aemeasurable_mult), fix a Borel function theta~ with theta~ = theta at H^n-a.e. point of M, and put N_theta := {x in M : theta(x) != theta~(x)}, an H^n-null set.

2. C^1 cover (Simon Ch. 3, Lemma 1.2). By V.countablyRectifiable, M is contained in M_0' union (union over j of F_j(R^n)) with H^n(M_0') = 0 and F_j : R^n -> R^(n+l) Lipschitz.
 (2a) C^1 approximation (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.5, applied to each coordinate function; printed proof): let F : R^n -> R be Lipschitz and epsilon > 0. By Rademacher's theorem (SimonGMT Chapter02.rademacher_ae_differentiableAt) F is differentiable on a set B with L^n(R^n minus B) = 0. By Lusin's theorem there is a closed set C contained in B with grad F restricted to C continuous and L^n(R^n minus C) < epsilon/2. For x, y in C let R(x,y) := (F(y) - F(x) - grad F(x).(y - x))/|x - y| and eta_k(x) := sup{|R(x,y)| : y in C cap B_{1/k}(x), y != x}; eta_k decreases to 0 pointwise on C (differentiability), so by Egoroff's theorem on the sets C cap B_j(0) there is a closed set A contained in C with L^n(R^n minus A) < epsilon on whose bounded subsets eta_k -> 0 uniformly, i.e. Whitney's condition 1.6(*) holds on A. Whitney's extension theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Thm 1.6; SimonGMT Chapter02.exists_contDiff_one_extension_of_whitney) gives g in C^1(R^n) with g = F and grad g = grad F on A, so L^n({F != g}) < epsilon.
 (2b) Hence for each j and i >= 1 there is G_ij in C^1(R^n; R^(n+l)) with L^n({F_j != G_ij}) < 1/i. With Z_j := R^n minus (union over i of {F_j = G_ij}) we get L^n(Z_j) = 0, hence H^n(F_j(Z_j)) <= (Lip F_j)^n L^n(Z_j) = 0, and F_j(R^n) is contained in F_j(Z_j) union (union over i of G_ij(R^n)).
 (2c) For a C^1 map G : R^n -> R^(n+l) let JG := sqrt(det(DG^T DG)); JG(v) = 0 iff DG(v) is not injective. The image of the critical set {JG = 0} is H^n-null (Sard-type consequence of the area formula; SimonGMT Chapter02.area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero). If JG(v) > 0, then by the inverse function theorem there is r_v > 0 such that G is injective with injective differential on B_{2 r_v}(v) and G restricted to B^o_{2 r_v}(v) is a homeomorphism onto its image; then N := G(B^o_{r_v}(v)) is an embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifold, it is sigma-compact (union of the compact sets G(B_{r_v - 1/k}(v))) hence Borel, H^n(N) <= integral_{B_{r_v}(v)} JG dL^n < infinity (area formula for the injective Lipschitz map G on B_{r_v}(v); SimonGMT Chapter02.injective_area_formula_lipschitz_simon), T_z N = DG(w)(R^n) for z = G(w), and z -> p_{T_z N} = DG(w)(DG(w)^T DG(w))^(-1) DG(w)^T with w = G^(-1)(z) is continuous on N. By the Lindelof property countably many such balls cover {JG > 0}.
 (2d) Collecting: M is contained in N_0 union (union over j >= 1 of N_j), where N_0 is a Borel set with H^n(N_0) = 0 (enlarge the null set to a Borel null set, H^n being Borel regular) and each N_j (j >= 1) is a Borel embedded n-dimensional C^1 submanifold with H^n(N_j) < infinity on which z -> p_{T_z N_j} is continuous.

3. Disjoint pieces (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.3; SimonGMT Chapter03.simon_remark_1_3_nullMeasurable). Put M_0 := M cap N_0 and M_j := (M cap N_j) minus (union over i < j of N_i) for j >= 1. These sets are pairwise disjoint and H^n-null-measurable (M is, the N_i are Borel), M is their union, H^n(M_0) = 0, and M_j is contained in N_j.

4. Blow-up of a C^1 submanifold. Let N be one of the N_j and x in N. Claim: for every f in C_c(R^(n+l)), lambda^(-n) integral_N f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z) -> integral_{T_x N} f dH^n as lambda -> 0+, and for each R > 0 the quantity lambda^(-n) H^n(N cap B_{R lambda}(x)) stays bounded as lambda -> 0+. Proof: choose an orthogonal map Q of R^(n+l) with Q(T_x N) = R^n x {0}. By the implicit function theorem (applied in a local parametrization G of N to w -> p_{T_x N}(G(w) - x), whose differential at G^(-1)(x) is invertible) there are r > 0, an open set W containing x and a C^1 map u : B^n_r(0) -> R^l with u(0) = 0, Du(0) = 0 and N cap W = {x + Q^(-1)(v, u(v)) : v in B^n_r(0)}; as N is embedded there is epsilon > 0 with N cap B_epsilon(x) contained in N cap W. Let f be supported in B_R(0) and 0 < lambda < epsilon/R. By the area formula for the injective Lipschitz graph map v -> (v, u(v)) (Jacobian J_u(v) = sqrt(det(I + Du(v)^T Du(v))), continuous with J_u(0) = 1) and the substitution v = lambda w,
 lambda^(-n) integral_N f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z) = integral_{B^n_{r/lambda}(0)} f(Q^(-1)(w, u(lambda w)/lambda)) J_u(lambda w) dw.
The integrand vanishes for |w| > R, and for |w| <= R we have u(lambda w)/lambda -> Du(0) w = 0 and J_u(lambda w) -> 1 uniformly, while f is bounded and uniformly continuous; hence the right side tends to integral_{R^n} f(Q^(-1)(w, 0)) dw = integral_{T_x N} f dH^n (H^n on the n-plane T_x N is the image of L^n under the isometry w -> Q^(-1)(w, 0); Mathlib normalizes mu_HE[n] to agree with volume on EuclideanSpace R (Fin n)). Choosing f >= 1 on B_R(0) gives the boundedness claim.

5. Lusin sets and upper-density sets (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(1)). Fix j >= 1 and m and put A_{j,m} := (M_j cap W_m) minus N_theta, so H^n(A_{j,m}) <= H^n(N_j) < infinity. By Lusin's theorem (Simon Ch. 1, 1.17; SimonGMT Chapter01 IsBorelRegularOuterMeasure.simon_theorem_1_17; H^n is Borel regular) applied to the Borel function theta~ on A_{j,m}, for each k there is a compact set K_{j,m,k} contained in A_{j,m} with H^n(A_{j,m} minus K_{j,m,k}) < 1/k and theta~ restricted to K_{j,m,k} continuous; on K_{j,m,k} we have theta = theta~, so theta restricted to K_{j,m,k} is continuous, and H^n(A_{j,m} minus (union over k of K_{j,m,k})) = 0. By the upper density theorem (Simon Ch. 1, Thm 3.6; SimonGMT Chapter01.simon_theorem_3_6), writing K := K_{j,m,k}:
 (i) applied to the finite Borel regular measure mu_m and the mu_m-measurable set M minus K: limsup_{lambda -> 0+} lambda^(-n) mu_m((M minus K) cap B_lambda(x)) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x outside M minus K, in particular for H^n-a.e. x in K;
 (ii) applied to the finite Borel regular measure H^n restricted to N_j and the set N_j minus K: limsup_{lambda -> 0+} lambda^(-n) H^n((N_j minus K) cap B_lambda(x)) = 0 for H^n-a.e. x in K.
Let E be the union, over all j >= 1, m, k, of the exceptional H^n-null sets of (i) and (ii) and of the sets A_{j,m} minus (union over k of K_{j,m,k}), together with M_0 and N_theta. Then H^n(E) = 0, and every x in M minus E lies in some K_{j,m,k}.

6. Existence of the weighted approximate tangent space (proof of Thm 1.6 '=>' combined with Remark 1.8(1), i.e. Thm 1.9 '=>'). Let x in M minus E, so x in K := K_{j,m,k}, contained in M_j cap W_m, for some j >= 1, m, k. Put P := T_x N_j, an n-dimensional subspace. Let f in C_c(R^(n+l)) be supported in B_R(0), and let lambda > 0 be so small that B_{R lambda}(x) is contained in W_m. The homothety z -> (z - x)/lambda maps H^n restricted to M onto lambda^n times H^n restricted to eta_{x,lambda}(M) (scaling law H^n(x + lambda S) = lambda^n H^n(S); Mathlib hausdorffMeasure_homothety_image), so y -> theta(x + lambda y) is a.e. measurable for H^n restricted to eta_{x,lambda}(M) (composition of the a.e.-measurable theta with this homothety), the integrand y -> f(y) theta(x + lambda y) is integrable there (bounded by sup|f| times theta(x + lambda y) on the blow-up of M cap B_{R lambda}(x), and integral_{M cap B_{R lambda}(x)} theta dH^n < infinity), and
 Lambda_lambda(f) = lambda^(-n) integral_M f((z - x)/lambda) theta(z) dH^n(z).
Split M as K union (M minus K):
 (a) |lambda^(-n) integral_{M minus K} f((z - x)/lambda) theta(z) dH^n(z)| <= sup|f| lambda^(-n) mu((M minus K) cap B_{R lambda}(x)) -> 0 by 5(i);
 (b) |lambda^(-n) integral_K f((z - x)/lambda) (theta(z) - theta(x)) dH^n(z)| <= sup|f| e(lambda) lambda^(-n) H^n(N_j cap B_{R lambda}(x)) -> 0, where e(lambda) := sup{|theta(z) - theta(x)| : z in K cap B_{R lambda}(x)} -> 0 by continuity of theta on K at x, and the last factor is bounded by Step 4;
 (c) theta(x) lambda^(-n) integral_K f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z) = theta(x) [lambda^(-n) integral_{N_j} f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z) - lambda^(-n) integral_{N_j minus K} f((z - x)/lambda) dH^n(z)] -> theta(x) [integral_P f dH^n - 0] by Step 4 and 5(ii).
Adding (a), (b), (c): Lambda_lambda(f) -> theta(x) integral_P f dH^n as lambda -> 0+. Together with finrank P = n this is exactly HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M theta x P. Since theta(x) > 0 (x in M), weighted approximate tangent spaces at x are unique (SimonGMT Chapter03.HasWeightedApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique), so by the definition of V.tangentProj, p_x = P.starProjection, the orthogonal projection onto the n-dimensional subspace P = T_x N_j. Since H^n(E) = 0, Step 1 gives (a).

7. Measurability (b). For each j >= 1 choose a Borel set B_j contained in M_j with H^n(M_j minus B_j) = 0 (M_j is H^n-null-measurable). Define q(x) := p_{T_x N_j} if x in B_j (j >= 1) and q(x) := 0 otherwise. Each map x -> p_{T_x N_j} is continuous on the Borel set N_j (Step 2) and the B_j are pairwise disjoint Borel sets, so q is Borel measurable; its values lie in the finite-dimensional, hence second countable, normed space of linear maps of R^(n+l), so q is strongly measurable. By Step 6, p_x = p_{T_x N_j} = q(x) for every x in B_j minus E, and M minus (union over j >= 1 of (B_j minus E)) is H^n-null. By Step 1, p = q mu-a.e., so x -> p_x is AEStronglyMeasurable with respect to mu.

8. Density (c) (Simon Ch. 3, Remark 1.8(2)). Let x in M minus E with P as in Step 6, and let 0 < epsilon < 1. Choose continuous compactly supported f_+, f_- : R^(n+l) -> [0,1] with f_+ = 1 on B_1(0), f_+ = 0 off B_{1+epsilon}(0), f_- = 1 on B_{1-epsilon}(0), f_- = 0 off B^o_1(0). Then f_- <= indicator of B_1(0) <= f_+, and since theta > 0 on M, the change of variables of Step 6 gives, for small lambda, Lambda_lambda(f_-) <= lambda^(-n) integral_{M cap B_lambda(x)} theta dH^n = lambda^(-n) mu(B_lambda(x)) <= Lambda_lambda(f_+). By Step 6, Lambda_lambda(f_+-) -> theta(x) integral_P f_+- dH^n, and omega_n (1-epsilon)^n = H^n(P cap B_{1-epsilon}(0)) <= integral_P f_- dH^n and integral_P f_+ dH^n <= H^n(P cap B_{1+epsilon}(0)) = omega_n (1+epsilon)^n (H^n on the n-plane P is n-dimensional Lebesgue measure and the unit ball of R^n has volume pi^(n/2)/Gamma(n/2+1) = omega_n, Mathlib EuclideanSpace.volume_ball). Hence theta(x) omega_n (1-epsilon)^n <= liminf lambda^(-n) mu(B_lambda(x)) <= limsup lambda^(-n) mu(B_lambda(x)) <= theta(x) omega_n (1+epsilon)^n, and letting epsilon -> 0, mu(B_lambda(x))/(omega_n lambda^n) -> theta(x) as lambda -> 0+. All quantities are finite and theta(x) > 0, so in [0,infinity] we get mu(closedBall x lambda)/ofReal(omega_n lambda^n) -> ofReal(theta(x)) as lambda -> 0+, i.e. V.HasDensity x (theta x). This holds for every x in M minus E, hence mu-a.e. by Step 1, which is (c).
proof_key_steps: Reduce (a)-(c) to H^n-a.e. x in M, localize to balls W_m with compact closure in U, and fix a Borel representative theta~ of theta (null set N_theta).

Lemma 1.2 (with the printed proof of the C^1 approximation theorem 1.5 of Ch. 2): cover M, up to an H^n-null Borel set, by countably many Borel embedded C^1 n-submanifolds N_j of finite H^n-measure (critical images are null; inverse function theorem).
Remark 1.3: split M into disjoint null-measurable pieces M_j contained in N_j.
Blow-ups of a C^1 submanifold at x converge to H^n on T_xN; local H^n-density of N is bounded.
Lusin compacts K_k with theta continuous; upper density theorem for mu restricted to M minus K_k and for H^n restricted to N_j minus K_k.
At H^n-a.e. x the weighted blow-up integrals converge to theta(x) times the integral over T_xN_j; uniqueness gives p_x = p_{T_xN_j}.
p agrees mu-a.e. with a Borel map assembled from the continuous maps x -> p_{T_xN_j}: AEStronglyMeasurable.
Remark 1.8(2): test functions squeezing the unit ball give mu(B_r(x))/(omega_n r^n) -> theta(x).

audit.reason: The type matches all three asserted conclusions and hypotheses. Localization, the C¹ cover, Lusin compact sets, and upper-density estimates establish the weighted tangent limit; uniqueness identifies tangentProj. The Borel representative and ball-squeezing arguments then prove measurability and density without assuming either conclusion.

subproblem.title: L^1 tilt-height estimate (Lemma A: L^1 form of the computation proving Simon 5.2.1)
subproblem.statement: Let n >= 1, l >= 0, U open in R^(n+l), V a RectifiableVarifold n l U with generalized mean curvature H in U, z in R^(n+l), r > 0 with B_r(z) contained in U, h >= 0, and T an n-dimensional subspace with dist(x - z, T) <= h for every x in spt V cap B_r(z). Then integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 144 r^(-2) integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu (Bochner integrals; |.| the Hilbert-Schmidt norm, i.e. hsNormSq).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the computation proving Simon, Ch. 5, Lemma 2.1 (pp. 107-108), kept in L^1 form (Lemma A of the parent proof, correction (b)): instead of absorbing the mean-curvature term by Cauchy-Schwarz (which produces integral |H|^2 and, via Remark 2.2, needs p >= 2), we use |x'| <= h. No lower bound on theta and no integrability exponent p are needed.

Notation: mu := V.weight; p_x := V.tangentProj x; for a linear map A of R^(n+l), |A|^2 := hsNormSq A = sum_i |A e_i|^2 = trace(A^* A), and ||A|| is the operator norm, so ||A|| <= |A|; p_T := T.starProjection and p_{T^perp} := I - p_T.

0. Preliminaries. B_r(z) is compact and contained in U, so mu(B_r(z)) < infinity (V.integrableOn_mult) and H is mu-integrable on B_r(z) (H is locally integrable on U). By aal_tangent_structure, for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace (symmetric, idempotent, trace n), and x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable. Also mu-a.e. x lies in spt V (mu(R^(n+l) minus spt mu) = 0 by Mathlib Measure.measure_compl_support, and mu(R^(n+l) minus U) = 0 because mu is concentrated on M contained in U). The function x -> |p_x - p_T|^2 is mu-a.e. strongly measurable and bounded (|p_x - p_T| <= |p_x| + |p_T| <= 2 sqrt(n + l)), and x -> dist(x - z, T)^2 is continuous and <= r^2 on B_r(z); hence all integrals in the statement are integrals of integrable functions on sets of finite measure.

1. Cutoff and test field. Fix phi in C^1(R; [0,1]) with phi = 1 on (-infinity, 1/2], phi = 0 on [1, infinity) and |phi'| <= 3 (possible since the transition interval has length 1/2 and 3 > 2; e.g. a C^1 smoothing of the piecewise linear function with slope -2). Put zeta(x) := phi(|x - z|/r); zeta is C^1 (phi is constant near 0), 0 <= zeta <= 1, zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z), zeta = 0 outside B^o_r(z), and |grad zeta| <= 3/r. Put x' := p_{T^perp}(x - z) = (x - z) - p_T(x - z), so |x'| = dist(x - z, T) (Mathlib Submodule.dist_starProjection_eq_infDist), and X(x) := zeta(x)^2 x'. X is C^1, has compact support, and tsupport X is contained in B_r(z), hence in U; so X is admissible in V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H.

2. Tangential divergence (Simon (1)-(3) in the proof of 2.1). DX(x) v = zeta^2 p_{T^perp} v + 2 zeta (grad zeta . v) x'. At every x where p_x is a rank-n orthogonal projection (mu-a.e.), since the trace of v -> (grad zeta . p_x v) x' equals grad zeta . p_x x' (p_x symmetric),
 div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) o p_x) = zeta^2 trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) + 2 zeta grad zeta . p_x x'.
Here trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) = trace(p_x) - trace(p_T p_x) = n - trace(p_T p_x), while |p_x - p_T|^2 = trace((p_x - p_T)^2) = trace(p_x) + trace(p_T) - 2 trace(p_T p_x) = 2n - 2 trace(p_T p_x); hence trace(p_{T^perp} p_x) = s(x) := (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2. Moreover p_T x' = 0, so p_x x' = (p_x - p_T) x'. Thus div_M X = zeta^2 s + 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' mu-a.e.

3. First variation. The functions zeta^2 s, zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x', and zeta^2 x' . H are mu-integrable (bounded measurable functions vanishing off B_r(z), resp. a bounded function times |H| on B_r(z)). The identity integral div_M X dmu = - integral X . H dmu gives
 integral zeta^2 s dmu = - integral 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x' dmu - integral zeta^2 x' . H dmu.

4. Absorption. |(p_x - p_T) x'| <= ||p_x - p_T|| |x'| <= |p_x - p_T| |x'| = sqrt(2 s) |x'|. With a := zeta sqrt(s) and b := sqrt(2) |grad zeta| |x'|, 2ab <= (1/2) a^2 + 2 b^2 gives |2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x'| <= 2 sqrt(2) zeta sqrt(s) |grad zeta| |x'| <= (1/2) zeta^2 s + 4 |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2. Therefore integral zeta^2 s <= (1/2) integral zeta^2 s + 4 integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 + integral zeta^2 |x'| |H|, and since integral zeta^2 s < infinity,
 integral zeta^2 s dmu <= 8 integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 dmu + 2 integral zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu.

5. Conclusion. Since zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}(z) and s >= 0, (1/2) integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= integral zeta^2 s dmu. Since |grad zeta|^2 <= 9/r^2 and grad zeta = 0 off B_r(z), 8 integral |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 dmu <= 72 r^(-2) integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu. Since zeta^2 <= indicator of B_r(z) and |x'| <= h for mu-a.e. x in B_r(z) (such x lie in spt V cap B_r(z), where dist(x - z, T) <= h by hypothesis), 2 integral zeta^2 |x'| |H| dmu <= 2 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu. Multiplying by 2:
 integral_{B_{r/2}(z)} |p_x - p_T|^2 dmu <= 144 r^(-2) integral_{B_r(z)} dist(x - z, T)^2 dmu + 4 h integral_{B_r(z)} |H| dmu,
which is the assertion (with |p_x - p_T|^2 = hsNormSq(V.tangentProj x - T.starProjection)).
proof_key_steps: aal_tangent_structure: p_x is a rank-n orthogonal projection mu-a.e. and measurable; all integrands are integrable on B_r(z).
Test field X = zeta^2 p_{T^perp}(x - z) with zeta = phi(|x-z|/r), |grad zeta| <= 3/r, tsupport in B_r(z).
div_M X = zeta^2 (1/2)|p_x - p_T|^2 + 2 zeta grad zeta . (p_x - p_T) x'.
First variation plus 2ab <= a^2/2 + 2b^2 absorbs the gradient term: int zeta^2 s <= 8 int |grad zeta|^2 |x'|^2 + 2 int zeta^2 |x'||H|.
Use zeta = 1 on B_{r/2}, |grad zeta| <= 3/r and |x'| <= h mu-a.e. on B_r(z).

subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon, Ch. 4, 3.2-3.6 (radial first variation and the epsilon-cutoff) and 4.1-4.8 (L^p mean curvature), with the coefficient in front of Lambda in 4.2 read as kappa = (p-n)/(4p) (the value required by the integration after 4.4; cf. SimonGMT Chapter04 lpMeanCurvatureKappa and LpAnnularCorrection), and with the passage epsilon -> 0 of the integrating factor carried out explicitly.

Notation (contract). mu := V.weight = theta H^n restricted to M (M = V.carrier, theta = V.mult); spt V := V.support = U cap spt mu; p_x := V.tangentProj x and p_x^perp v := v - p_x v; B_s(y) := closedBall y s (closed), B^o_s(y) := ball y s (open); omega_n := unitBallVolume n > 0; for z and s > 0, K(z,s) := V.scaledLpNorm H p z s = (s^(p-n) integral_{B_s(z)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p) in [0,infinity]; kappa := (p-n)/(4p) > 0; g_y(x) := |x - y - p_x(x - y)|^2 / |x - y|^(n+2) (= 0 at x = y by the convention a/0 = 0). Also r(x) := |x - y|, nu(x) := (x - y)/r(x) and D^perp r(x) := p_x^perp nu(x) for x != y, and D^perp r(y) := 0, so that g_y(x) = |D^perp r(x)|^2 / r(x)^n for x != y (and both sides are 0 at x = y). For 0 < t <= S write ||H||_t := (integral_{B_t(y)} |H|^p dmu)^(1/p).

0. Preliminaries. By aal_tangent_structure (n >= 1, U open): for mu-a.e. x, p_x is the orthogonal projection onto an n-dimensional subspace (so p_x is symmetric, idempotent, trace p_x = n, |p_x v| <= |v|, and |p_x nu|^2 + |p_x^perp nu|^2 = |nu|^2 = 1), and x -> p_x is mu-a.e. strongly measurable, so g_y and all integrands below are mu-a.e. strongly measurable. B_S(y) is compact and contained in U, so mu(B_S(y)) < infinity (V.integrableOn_mult), and H is mu-integrable on B_S(y) (H is locally integrable on U, part of V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature). By hypothesis ||H||_S < infinity; t -> ||H||_t is nondecreasing, and ||H||_R = R^(n/p - 1) K(y,R) <= R^(n/p - 1) kappa Lambda (because K(y,R) = (R^(p-n) ||H||_R^p)^(1/p) = R^(1 - n/p) ||H||_R).
 Integrability in (ii): if 0 < s <= r <= R, then on B_r(y) minus B_s(y) we have r(x) > s, hence 0 <= g_y(x) <= |x - y|^2/|x - y|^(n+2) < s^(-n) for mu-a.e. such x (|p_x^perp v| <= |v|); as mu(B_r(y)) < infinity and g_y is a.e. strongly measurable, g_y is mu-integrable on B_r(y) minus B_s(y).

1. Cutoffs. Fix chi in C^1(R) nonincreasing with chi = 1 on (-infinity, 0] and chi = 0 on [1, infinity). For epsilon in (0,1] let phi_epsilon(t) := chi((t - 1)/epsilon): phi_epsilon is C^1, nonincreasing, 0 <= phi_epsilon <= 1, phi_epsilon = 1 on (-infinity, 1], phi_epsilon = 0 on [1 + epsilon, infinity), and for every t, phi_epsilon(t) -> indicator of (-infinity, 1] at t as epsilon -> 0+ (for t > 1 it is 0 once epsilon < t - 1).

2. Radial first variation (Simon 3.2, 4.1). Fix epsilon in (0,1] and rho > 0 with (1 + epsilon) rho < S. Let X(x) := phi_epsilon(r(x)/rho)(x - y). X equals x - y on B^o_rho(y) (phi_epsilon = 1 on (-infinity,1]) and is a composition of C^1 maps on the complement of {y}, so X is C^1; it vanishes outside B_{(1+epsilon) rho}(y), so it has compact support and tsupport X is contained in B_{(1+epsilon) rho}(y), which is contained in B_S(y) and hence in U. For x != y, DX(x) v = phi_epsilon(r/rho) v + rho^(-1) phi_epsilon'(r/rho) (nu . v)(x - y). At mu-a.e. x (where p_x is a rank-n orthogonal projection), using that the trace of v -> (nu . p_x v) w equals p_x nu . w,
 div_M X(x) = trace(DX(x) o p_x) = n phi_epsilon(r/rho) + (r/rho) phi_epsilon'(r/rho) (1 - |D^perp r|^2)
(at x = y the second term is absent because phi_epsilon' = 0 on (-infinity,1)). The definition of generalized mean curvature (V.HasGeneralizedMeanCurvature H, applicable to X) gives
 integral [n phi_epsilon(r/rho) + (r/rho) phi_epsilon'(r/rho)(1 - |D^perp r|^2)] dmu = - integral phi_epsilon(r/rho)(x - y) . H dmu. (2.1)
For 0 < rho < S/(1 + epsilon) put I(rho) := integral phi_epsilon(r/rho) dmu, J(rho) := integral phi_epsilon(r/rho)|D^perp r|^2 dmu, L(rho) := integral phi_epsilon(r/rho)(x - y) . H dmu (finite). The rho-derivative of phi_epsilon(r/rho) is -(r/rho^2) phi_epsilon'(r/rho), which is bounded uniformly for rho in compact subintervals and supported in B_S(y) (finite measure); by differentiation under the integral sign I and J are C^1 with I'(rho) = - integral (r/rho^2) phi_epsilon'(r/rho) dmu >= 0 and J'(rho) = - integral (r/rho^2) phi_epsilon'(r/rho) |D^perp r|^2 dmu >= 0, and L is continuous by dominated convergence (|phi_epsilon(r/rho)(x - y) . H| <= S |H| on B_S(y)). Since (r/rho) phi_epsilon'(r/rho) = - rho d/drho[phi_epsilon(r/rho)], (2.1) says n I - rho I' + rho J' = - L, i.e.
 d/drho (rho^(-n) I(rho)) = rho^(-n) J'(rho) + rho^(-n-1) L(rho). (2.2)

3. Hoelder estimate (Simon 4.2-4.3 with kappa = (p-n)/(4p)). As phi_epsilon(r/rho) = 0 for r >= (1+epsilon) rho and 0 <= phi_epsilon <= 1 (so phi_epsilon^(p/(p-1)) <= phi_epsilon), Hoelder's inequality gives |L(rho)| <= (1+epsilon) rho integral_{B_{(1+epsilon)rho}(y)} |H| phi_epsilon(r/rho) dmu <= (1+epsilon) rho ||H||_{(1+epsilon)rho} I(rho)^(1-1/p). Using a^(1-1/p) <= 1 + a (a >= 0),
 |rho^(-n-1) L(rho)| <= (1+epsilon) ||H||_{(1+epsilon)rho} rho^(-n/p) (rho^(-n) I(rho))^(1-1/p) <= (1+epsilon) ||H||_{(1+epsilon)rho} rho^(-n/p) (1 + rho^(-n) I(rho)).
Define a_epsilon(rho) := rho^(-n-1) L(rho) / (1 + rho^(-n) I(rho)), continuous on (0, S/(1+epsilon)), with
 |a_epsilon(rho)| <= (1+epsilon) ||H||_{(1+epsilon) rho} rho^(-n/p) <= 2 ||H||_S rho^(-n/p). (3.1)
Since n/p < 1, rho^(-n/p) is integrable near 0. Now (2.2) reads d/drho (1 + rho^(-n) I) = rho^(-n) J' + a_epsilon (1 + rho^(-n) I).

4. Integrating factor (Simon 4.4) and squeeze (Simon 3.5). For 0 < rho < S/(1+epsilon) let F_epsilon(rho) := exp(- integral_0^rho a_epsilon(t) dt); F_epsilon is C^1 with F_epsilon' = - a_epsilon F_epsilon, hence d/drho [F_epsilon(rho)(1 + rho^(-n) I(rho))] = F_epsilon(rho) rho^(-n) J'(rho) >= 0 and, for 0 < sigma <= rho < S/(1+epsilon),
 F_epsilon(rho)(1 + rho^(-n) I(rho)) - F_epsilon(sigma)(1 + sigma^(-n) I(sigma)) = integral_sigma^rho F_epsilon(t) t^(-n) J'(t) dt =: D_epsilon(sigma,rho). (4.1)
By Tonelli (the integrand F_epsilon(t) t^(-n) (-(r/t^2) phi_epsilon'(r/t)) |D^perp r|^2 is >= 0), D_epsilon(sigma,rho) = integral |D^perp r(x)|^2 [integral_sigma^rho F_epsilon(t) t^(-n) d/dt(phi_epsilon(r/t)) dt] dmu(x). For fixed x with r = r(x) > 0, d/dt(phi_epsilon(r/t)) = -(r/t^2) phi_epsilon'(r/t) >= 0 vanishes unless r/(1+epsilon) <= t <= r, where r^(-n) <= t^(-n) <= (1+epsilon)^n r^(-n), and integral_sigma^rho d/dt(phi_epsilon(r/t)) dt = phi_epsilon(r/rho) - phi_epsilon(r/sigma) >= 0. With c_epsilon(rho) := integral_0^rho |a_epsilon(t)| dt we have e^(-c_epsilon(rho)) <= F_epsilon(t) <= e^(c_epsilon(rho)) for 0 < t <= rho. Hence
 e^(-c_epsilon(rho)) A_epsilon(sigma,rho) <= D_epsilon(sigma,rho) <= e^(c_epsilon(rho)) (1+epsilon)^n A_epsilon(sigma,rho), (4.2)
where A_epsilon(sigma,rho) := integral r^(-n) (phi_epsilon(r/rho) - phi_epsilon(r/sigma)) |D^perp r|^2 dmu (integrand := 0 at x = y).

5. Letting epsilon -> 0 (Simon 3.6, 4.5-4.7). Fix a nonincreasing sequence epsilon_k -> 0+ with epsilon_1 <= 1 and (1 + epsilon_1) R < S (e.g. epsilon_k := epsilon_1/k), so that (1 + epsilon_k) R < S for every k, and write I_k, L_k, a_k, F_k, c_k, D_k, A_k for the objects above with epsilon = epsilon_k; all are defined for radii in (0, R].
 (5a) For t in (0, R]: I_k(t) -> mu(B_t(y)) and L_k(t) -> L_0(t) := integral_{B_t(y)} (x - y) .
